name: Jaekelopterus
description: Large pterygotid eurypterid with acute lateral eyes, robust toothed chelicerae, four walking-limb pairs, swimming paddles, twelve trunk rings and a triangular keeled telson.
notes: Initial preview reconstruction; pigmentation and soft anatomy are artistic.
1.8 m is a representative display assumption; the famous roughly 2.5 m giant estimate is extrapolated from an isolated chelicera, not a complete giant body.
Four slender non-chelate walking pairs plus pair VI swimming paddles; enlarged chelicerae are pair I. No invented scorpion sting or venom anatomy.
Rhenaniae claw and eye evidence is distinguished from comparative Jaekelopterus howelli postcranial material.
Moult is a preparatory articulated extension without shell splitting or body scaling. Precise locomotor cycles are inferred, not fossil-observed.
Full regional pigment is multiplied once by near-neutral UV albedo; LOD bakes that factor once without textures.
